summary: Benaka, Inc. is a New Brunswick, NJ general contractor founded in 1994 that performs design-build, bid-build, JOC/MATOC, IDIQ and maintenance-and-repair work, mostly for federal agencies (Air Force, Army, Navy, DoL, Smithsonian) plus institutional and medical clients across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. It holds federal IDIQ vehicles, including a multi-award construction contract with the Air Force at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst and a 2026 Army Corps of Engineers small-business MATOC, and appears to run a lean office with a single email-based careers/vendor intake. Its public profile suggests heavy USACE/Air Force quality-control documentation (submittals, RFIs, daily QC reports, three-phase control) done by a small in-house staff - the clearest place AI support would pay off.

facts.fact: Founded in 1994; positions itself as a full-service general contractor offering Design Build, Bid Build Firm Fixed Price, Job Order Contracts (JOC), IDIQ and Maintenance & Repair (M&R) contracts.
Office is at 7 Lawrence Street, New Brunswick, NJ 08901; main line 732-246-7060, fax 732-246-7073, email benaka@benakainc.com; office hours Monday-Friday 9:00am-5:00pm.

Client list includes U.S. Dept. of Air Force, Army, Navy, Dept. of Labor, U.S. Postal Service, Smithsonian Institution, Baltimore Orioles organization, Prince George's County MD school district and various NJ/NY/MD municipal agencies.
Geographic range is the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic: contracts in Maine, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, upstate NY, NYC, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia and DC.

About page says the project management team is supported by in-house Estimators, Contract Specialists and Finance professionals at the corporate office, and that work is executed in fully occupied facilities with concurrent multi-discipline projects.

Federal procurement records list BENAKA INC. (UEI CHFAPANM3SA7, CAGE 1RGV1) at 7 Lawrence St, New Brunswick NJ, incorporated in New Jersey, minority-owned (Subcontinent Asian American) and self-certified small disadvantaged business; it holds IDIQ/MACC vehicle FA448420D0005 with Air Force 87 CONS at the $134M base-and-all-options level and a 2025 modification on that vehicle.

In 2026 the company was added to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (New England District) Small Business Construction MATOC pool with a shared $90M ceiling and an estimated completion date of Aug. 10, 2031; nine bids were received.
LinkedIn company page describes Benaka, Inc. as a privately held civil-engineering/construction firm in New Brunswick, NJ, founded 1994, 11-50 employees, and states it is 8(a) certified.
Third-party firmographic estimate puts Benaka at roughly $22.5M annual revenue and about 98 employees (estimate, not company-reported).
Third-party lead directory lists Benaka under General Building Contractors with SBE and MBE qualifications on file.

The careers page currently advertises one role - Quality Control Manager for Tri-State federal projects inside military installations, contingent on federal security clearance - with resumes accepted by email.

A live Benaka job posting for Construction Quality Control Manager/Project Superintendent lists a $100,000-$140,000 salary, 401(k) with match, health insurance and PTO, and requires daily commuting to the federal project site.

operations_signals: Inbound contact is phone (732-246-7060), fax, email or a web contact form; no online booking, quote request or bid portal is published (https://www.benakainc.com/contact-us.html).

Office hours are Monday-Friday 9:00am-5:00pm, while project sites span the Northeast/Mid-Atlantic and the current QC posting requires daily commuting and travel - so field/office coverage gaps outside 9-5 are plausible but not stated (https://www.benakainc.com/contact-us.html).

Subcontractor/vendor onboarding is manual: interested subs are asked to email their details and expertise, with no vendor portal or prequalification form (https://www.benakainc.com/subcontractors.html).
Job intake is a single careers page with one open role and a 'send resumes to' email address - no ATS or application form (https://www.benakainc.com/careers.html).

Field operations are documentation-heavy by design: daily pre-work safety briefings, continuous safety inspections with checklists, and QC documentation from bid preparation through construction (https://www.benakainc.com/about-us.html).

Federal work is competitively bid - the Air Force MACC award shows 28 offers received on the underlying solicitation, indicating high-volume proposal preparation (https://www.fpds.gov/ezsearch/FEEDS/ATOM?FEEDNAME=PUBLIC&templateName=1.5.3&q=Benaka+SIGNED_DATE%3A%5B2023%2F01%2F01%2C2026%2F12%2F31%5D).
Work is performed inside fully occupied government facilities, requiring phased scheduling and coordination with facility owners (https://www.benakainc.com/about-us.html).
hiring_signals: Open Quality Control Manager role: coordinates with Superintendent, SSHO and PM on scheduling, delivery and logistics; manages the three phases of control and all associated report forms; runs preparatory meetings and initial inspections; keeps QC/production meeting minutes; writes RFIs with the PM; prepares purchase orders before ordering material; completes daily production reports; weekly toolbox talks (https://www.benakainc.com/careers.html).

Posting asks for familiarity with QCS/RMS project management software (USACE/Air Force construction management systems) and proficiency with Microsoft Office/Project and web-based programs - i.e., reporting is done in multiple disconnected systems (https://www.benakainc.com/careers.html).

Employment is contingent on federal security clearance / background check for access to military installations, adding a compliance and credentialing step to every hire (https://www.benakainc.com/careers.html).

Public postings combine two jobs into one - 'Quality Control Manager/Project Superintendent' - for multiple federal construction projects, suggesting lean field staffing and multitasking roles (https://www.simplyhired.com/job/m2NUtDE885oLWMoDsU45Bi_gsBQWD8D19S_eYPt48YmnNXahaaHWWQ).

Additional QC Manager openings appear for specific locations such as Newport, RI, indicating project-driven hiring spread across the region (https://www.glassdoor.com/job-listing/construction-quality-control-manager-project-superintendent-federal-construction-benaka-inc-JV_IC1151279_KO0,80_KE81,91.htm?jl=1009968021406).

Support staff cited on the About page (estimators, contract specialists, finance) is the group most exposed to repetitive proposal, compliance and billing paperwork (https://www.benakainc.com/about-us.html).
review_themes: No third-party customer reviews were found: BuildZoom reports no reviews for the contractor, and BBB/Yelp/Google review pages could not be retrieved (403 or no profile content) (https://www.buildzoom.com/contractor/benaka-inc).

BBB profile exists for 'Commercial Contractors' in New Brunswick and is described in search results as not BBB-accredited; rating, complaint and review counts could not be read (https://www.bbb.org/us/nj/new-brunswick/profile/commercial-contractors/benaka-inc-0221-90103199).

Company-published commendation letters (not independent reviews) from Navy, Army, Air Force and school-district staff repeatedly praise on-time or early completion, cooperation with government schedule constraints, responsiveness to submittal comments, and QC/safety team performance (https://www.benakainc.com/commendations.html).

Those same company-published letters emphasize document handling - submittal review responses, meeting communication, change orders - as the visible quality differentiator, which is also where client dissatisfaction would surface (https://www.benakainc.com/commendations.html).

Employee-review signals are thin and inconclusive: Glassdoor shows 4 Benaka reviews and Indeed shows an employer page with Q&A, but both blocked retrieval so themes cannot be summarized (https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Benaka-Reviews-E279727.htm).
tech_footprint: Website is a static HTML template with no CMS-driven content, no chat widget, no client portal and no online forms beyond a basic contact form; content last refreshed around a '25 Year Anniversary' banner (https://www.benakainc.com/).
Employee email runs on Microsoft Exchange/OWA at bimail.benakainc.com/owa, linked from the contact page (https://www.benakainc.com/contact-us.html).

Field QC reporting depends on external government systems (QCS/RMS) plus Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and Project - export/re-key work between them is likely (https://www.benakainc.com/careers.html).
Marketing presence is limited to a Facebook page and LinkedIn company page; no published case studies, blog, newsroom or downloadable capability data (https://www.benakainc.com/).
Company publishes project and client galleries as static pages rather than structured data, so past-performance retrieval for proposals is manual (https://www.benakainc.com/sitemap.xml).
Still lists a fax line as a primary contact channel, consistent with a paper/email-heavy federal contracting workflow (https://www.benakainc.com/contact-us.html).
growth_signals: Added in 2026 to the USACE New England District Small Business Construction MATOC (shared $90M ceiling, five-year ordering period, orders typically $500K-$10M, estimated completion 2031) - expands federal design-build pipeline (https://www.highergov.com/news/benaka-joins-90-million-army-corps-small-business-6490041).

Already on an earlier Corps small-construction design-build pool, where it received an ~$8.2M order to repair the fuel-cell hangar at Barnes Air National Guard Base, MA (https://www.highergov.com/news/benaka-joins-90-million-army-corps-small-business-6490041).

Holds an Air Force MACC IDIQ at JBMDL (FA448420D0005) with $134M base-and-all-options value and continued modifications through 2025, indicating recurring task-order volume (https://www.fpds.gov/ezsearch/FEEDS/ATOM?FEEDNAME=PUBLIC&templateName=1.5.3&q=Benaka+SIGNED_DATE%3A%5B2023%2F01%2F01%2C2026%2F12%2F31%5D).

Company claims growth 'steadily ever since' 1994 and emphasizes repeat business, exercised options and contract plus-ups as evidence of customer satisfaction (https://www.benakainc.com/about-us.html).

Won a design-build MACC order extension at JBMDL (FA448422F0104, ~$360K total obligated) showing ongoing task-order execution (https://www.fpds.gov/ezsearch/FEEDS/ATOM?FEEDNAME=PUBLIC&templateName=1.5.3&q=Benaka+SIGNED_DATE%3A%5B2023%2F01%2F01%2C2026%2F12%2F31%5D).
Hiring a QC manager for Tri-State work while bidding New England Corps work suggests geographic expansion beyond its historical New Jersey/Navy-Yard core (https://www.benakainc.com/careers.html).
decision_maker: Unknown - no owner, president or GM is named on the company website (home, about, contact, careers pages) or its LinkedIn company page as retrieved; the only named individuals on the site are client references.

inferences.inference: Proposal and compliance production is likely the largest repetitive workload relative to headcount.
inferences.reasoning: The firm pursues multiple federal vehicles (Air Force MACC, USACE MATOC, JOC/IDIQ) where each bid needs past-performance write-ups, submittal registers and compliance matrices, and the About page says this is handled by a small in-house estimating/contract-specialist group.

inferences.inference: Quality-control paperwork is a strong AI-assist candidate.
inferences.reasoning: The job description lists minutes, daily QC/production reports, RFIs, purchase orders, submittal register management and three-phase control forms as core duties for a role the firm has to hire externally at $100K-$140K; much of that is drafting and reconciling structured text.

inferences.inference: Inbound vendor, subcontractor and applicant handling is unautomated.
inferences.reasoning: Subs and job seekers are told to email the general inbox with no form, portal or ATS, so qualification, sorting and follow-up fall to office staff.

inferences.inference: After-hours responsiveness is probably weak for non-federal inquiries.
inferences.reasoning: Published hours are 9-5 Monday-Friday with phone/fax/email and no after-hours line, chat or self-service scheduling; this is an inference since no call data or review complaints were available.

inferences.inference: The company may be larger than its LinkedIn band (11-50) suggests.
inferences.reasoning: ZoomInfo and Kona Equity both estimate ~98 employees and ~$22.5M revenue, and the firm executes concurrent multi-state federal projects; these are third-party estimates, not confirmed.

inferences.inference: 8(a) status may be a marketing claim rather than current certification.
inferences.reasoning: LinkedIn says 'currently 8(a) certified', while FPDS records show self-certified small disadvantaged business with isSBACertified8AProgramParticipant false; status should be verified before relying on it for set-aside positioning.

data_gaps: Decision-maker name/title: not published on the company's own site or company page; only client-reference names appear publicly.

Review data: BBB (403), Google/Yelp (no retrievable profile content), Glassdoor (403), Indeed (403) and BuildZoom (403 on profile fetch; search snippet says no reviews) - no verified customer or employee review themes.
Job posting dates and full current board coverage: Indeed, Glassdoor and LinkedIn jobs pages blocked; posting dates for the QC Manager roles could not be confirmed.
Headcount: conflicting third-party figures (LinkedIn 11-50; ZoomInfo/Kona ~98 employees, ~$22.5M revenue); no company-reported number.
No local news coverage (NJBIZ, local papers) about the firm was found through available search providers.
FederalCompass and war.gov contract pages returned no readable content (JS-rendered / 403), so the FY25 JBMDL MACC award (FA448425D0009) could not be independently verified beyond a search snippet.
Web search providers were partially rate-limited/blocked during this run (Exa, OpenAI, DuckDuckGo, BBB, Indeed, Glassdoor), so coverage is narrower than planned.
